messages:
maria: Heads up — saw a sustained p99 latency spike on AWQ-serve when act-quant enabled with group_size=96 under 120c concurrency. Repro steps and logs below.
jonathan: Ugh. Was that the canary rollout? Which model and sequence lengths?
sara: Model: redwood/open-7b-v2 (AWQ, act-quant=on). Mostly seq_len 1024. Canary at ~5% traffic on dedicated pool. p99 jumped from 220ms to ~1.1s then some OOM-ish traces.
lee: Sharing tail of pod logs: ```
[2026-03-19T21:03:12Z] INFO serving: request received id=... seq=1024
[2026-03-19T21:03:12Z] WARN awq.kvcache: cache miss, fallback path
[2026-03-19T21:03:13Z] ERROR runtime: aten::mul out of range (nan) at aten_ops.cpp:221
[2026-03-19T21:03:13Z] WARN gpu: memory spike, allocated 5.6GB, free 0.2GB
```
ben: Looks like numeric instability from activation quantization hitting large dynamic ranges when group_size is large. AWQ grouping tries to fold quant ranges across many tokens — greater groups -> more aggressive compression.
maria: Quick experiment notes: switched to group_size=32 + act_clamp=6.0, restarted canary -> p99 back to ~240ms, no OOMs in 30m. But model perplexity on golden-set increased slightly (+0.8% perplexity).
jonathan: Do we have a reproducible eval run that mimics production concurrency? Can we perf/eval on a dedicated node with same batch distribution?
eval-bot: ran golden-set eval (1000 prompts) on awq config variants. Results: 
- group=96, actq=on: accuracy_delta = -3.2% on extractive QA suite, p99 latency = 1.05s
- group=32, actq=on, act_clamp=6.0: accuracy_delta = -0.6%, p99 = 0.24s
- group=32, actq=off (GPTQ fallback): accuracy_delta = +0.1%, p99 = 0.40s
lee: So tradeoff space: fewer groups = better numeric stability and accuracy at cost of slightly higher latency than extreme grouping, but still good. Also GPTQ fallback looks safe but slower.
sara: For serving profile I'd propose: primary config group_size=32, act_clamp=6.0, per-request timeout 3s, and fallback policy to GPTQ-4bit for failures. Canary rollout plan: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% with golden-set checks after each step.
maria: Added small config diff for runtime: ```diff
- awq_group_size: 96
- awq_act_quant: true
+ awq_group_size: 32
+ awq_act_quant: true
+ awq_act_clamp: 6.0
+ awq_fallback: gptq_4bit
```
ben: Also enable eval hooks in the console so any drift >1.5% triggers auto-rollback. And add a short-term mitigation: if p95 latency > 600ms for 5m, scale down canary and redirect to stable pool.
jonathan: Can infra add a temporary resource cap on canary pods (mem 8Gi) to catch OOMs earlier and fail fast?
deploy-bot: canary deployment started: model=open-7b-v2 awq-config=group32-actclamp6 canary=0.5%
lee: Let's also capture a few failing traces and an N=10 sample of prompts that triggered regressions. I'll push to the bakeoff folder and link in the ticket.
sara: Thanks — plan sounds good. I'll own the rollout and golden-set validation. If we see any >2% QA regressions or p99 > 600ms we'll rollback to GPTQ fallback. :thumbsup:
